sensitivity_null_tradeoff.description: No tradeoff exists: ALL alphas fail C1. Entropy-rate CMI does not bypass per-stratum KL bias.
sensitivity_null_tradeoff.crossover_alpha: none (no alpha achieves both C1 and C3)

C1-NULL-CONTROL.description: Shuffled-action within-session null, 500 permutations per alpha. |mean| < 0.1 bits.
C1-NULL-CONTROL.expected: |shuffled-action null_mean| < 0.1 bits for at least one alpha
C1-NULL-CONTROL.observed: All alphas fail: alpha=0.1 |mean|=0.240, alpha=0.5 |mean|=0.200, alpha=1.0 |mean|=0.275. No alpha passes C1.

C3-POSITIVE-CONTROL.description: Positive control CMI >= 0.5 bits with permutation p <= 0.001 for any alpha passing C1.
C3-POSITIVE-CONTROL.observed: Alpha=0.1 passes C3 (K3=0.523, p=0.001) but fails C1. Alpha=0.5 K3=-0.070 and alpha=1.0 K3=-0.186 both fail C3.

B-ENTROPY-RATE-DEG.description: Entropy-rate CMI on deterministic SPA where H(Y|Z,A)=0 by construction (deterministic transitions). Expected CMI = H(Y|Z) > 0.
B-ENTROPY-RATE-DEG.observed: Alpha=0.1 K3=0.544 passes threshold. Alpha=0.5 K3=-0.073 and alpha=1.0 K3=-0.199 are negative due to Laplace smoothing bias inflating H(Y|Z,A) above H(Y|Z).

observations: Entropy-rate CMI does NOT bypass the per-stratum KL bias-variance tradeoff. ALL three tested alphas (0.1, 0.5, 1.0) fail C1 (|shuffled-action null_mean| >= 0.1 bits): alpha=0.1 |mean|=0.240, alpha=0.5 |mean|=0.200, alpha=1.0 |mean|=0.275.

At alpha=0.1, the estimator achieves C3 sensitivity (K3=0.523 bits >= 0.5 threshold, p=0.001) but null centering fails at 2.4x threshold. This is the same tradeoff pattern as plug-in KL: sensitivity and null centering remain irreconcilable.

At alpha=0.5 and alpha=1.0, the entropy-rate CMI becomes NEGATIVE (K3=-0.070 and -0.186 respectively), meaning H(Y|Z,A) > H(Y|Z). This is a Laplace smoothing artifact: smoothing inflates H(Y|Z,A) more than H(Y|Z) because the (z,a) conditioning space has more cells than the z-only space, and pseudo-counts add artificial uncertainty proportionally to cell count.

The deterministic SPA positive control (B-ENTROPY-RATE-DEG) confirms the smoothing bias: alpha=0.1 K3=0.544 (correct, H(Y|Z)>0 by construction), but alpha=0.5 K3=-0.073 and alpha=1.0 K3=-0.199 are negative. The estimator fails on the very control where I(Y;A|Z)=0 by construction.

Stratum size decomposition (alpha=0.5): 343 strata in 5-9 bucket (observed CMI 0.117, null 0.079), 37 strata in 10-19 bucket (observed 0.240, null 0.130). Smaller strata contribute more null bias, same pattern as plug-in KL.
The null mean is stable across shuffles (std 0.0001-0.002), confirming the bias is systematic, not random. The null distribution is tightly concentrated away from zero.
K3-K2 differences remain positive across all alphas (0.192, 0.112, 0.082), suggesting the beyond-Markov signal exists in the data but the estimator cannot separate it from bias.
Design verification passes: 48/48 (state,action) pairs with 4 distinct candidates, 2 non-empty stratum size buckets.
validity_notes: The experiment uses the same 12-state stochastic SPA design as parent EXP-PHYSICS-35530591329. Results are specific to this SPA class.

Entropy-rate CMI computes H(Y|Z) - H(Y|Z,A) globally via histogram with Laplace smoothing. The global computation does not avoid the bias because Laplace smoothing adds pseudo-counts proportional to the number of cells, and H(Y|Z,A) has n_z * n_a * n_y cells while H(Y|Z) has n_z * n_y cells.
The negative CMI values at alpha >= 0.5 are a mathematical artifact of Laplace smoothing, not evidence against the true CMI being positive. The true I(Y;A|Z) = 1.52 bits is audit-confirmed.
The null control uses within-session action-label shuffle (500 permutations), same framework as parent.
Phase 2 (beyond-Markov K3-K2) was not executed because no alpha passes both C1 and C3.
All measurements are on synthetic in-memory SPA simulation. No browser/network/model calls.
The frozen decision rule FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING triggers on C1: all alphas have |null_mean| >= 0.1 bits. This is a valid scientific negative, not an infrastructure failure.
unresolved: Whether the entropy-rate CMI null bias is fundamental to Laplace-smoothed histogram estimation or can be resolved by (a) larger N, (b) kernel density estimation, (c) Bayesian entropy estimation, or (d) different smoothing (Jeffreys, Hellinger).
Whether the negative CMI at alpha >= 0.5 indicates that Laplace smoothing is categorically unsuitable for entropy-rate CMI on discrete spaces with many cells.
Whether the beyond-Markov K3-K2 signal (consistently positive 0.08-0.19 bits across alphas) can be detected by an estimator that does not suffer from the smoothing bias.
Whether Bayesian model comparison (action-dependent vs action-independent transition model via Bayes factor) detects the signal with valid null centering, as suggested by the parent handoff.
Whether likelihood-ratio tests between nested Markov and beyond-Markov models bypass the bias.
Whether production Web transitions with continuous state representations or larger vocabularies exhibit different bias characteristics.
Whether the 0.192-bit K3-K2 difference at alpha=0.1 is statistically significant or an artifact of the same smoothing bias affecting H(Y|Z) and H(Y|Z,A) differently.
